why_it_matters: the real capex - decides whether 250,000 even covers it or is one funding slice
pool_expansion_example: construction bid + design/permits + a contingency % (pools commonly carry 10-20% contingency)

why_it_matters: when cash leaves vs when revenue starts - drives payback and the 13-week forecast
pool_expansion_example: construction months and target opening date (miss the summer season and year-1 revenue halves)

why_it_matters: how much of the 250,000 is used and what joins it - changes the return ON THE 250,000
pool_expansion_example: share from this cash vs restricted gifts, campaign, or borrowing at 7.00%

why_it_matters: the return numerator - must be NEW money, not moved money
pool_expansion_example: added memberships x dues, swim-lesson seats x fee, rentals, camp add-ons - price x expected units each

why_it_matters: the return denominator's partner - pools are operating-cost heavy
pool_expansion_example: lifeguards/staff, chemicals, utilities, insurance, routine maintenance

why_it_matters: spreads the capex over the years it serves and reserves for renewal
pool_expansion_example: years of service; resurfacing/equipment cycle and its cost

why_it_matters: turns the revenue forecast from hope into a forecast
pool_expansion_example: waitlists, the tab-15 community-study findings, current aquatics utilization

why_it_matters: new revenue that replaces existing revenue is not a return
pool_expansion_example: does pool revenue pull families from existing programs?

why_it_matters: the framework weights mission 30% - the board must score it, not the model
pool_expansion_example: how central is aquatics to the JSV mission?

why_it_matters: restricted money changes what the 250,000 must cover and what may fund operations
pool_expansion_example: any gift restricted to the pool, and its timing/terms

why_it_matters: schedule and cost risk unique to construction
for a program the grid shifts utilization and fees, not interest rates
pool_expansion_example: verdict at 70/85/100% of forecast enrollment and at +/-10% fees
